note: I022 A Game Developer at Sea: a tiny fictional game made in the cabin. Each session is one task with one small choice; a wise choice counts double. Points are earned for the hours actually worked (an interrupted session counts its share). Read by src/core/pastimes.gd.

milestones.name: The keeper walks
milestones.log: The little keeper can walk up the spiral stairs now. She stops at the top to look at the sea, which I did not program. I am choosing to call it a feature.

milestones.name: The light turns
milestones.log: The lamp turns! It sweeps across the sea and every boat in the harbour blinks back. Tried it with the cabin lights off. Very pleased.

milestones.name: Ships to guide
milestones.log: Three little ships now sail home if the light finds them in time. The cat watched the first one arrive and approved.

milestones.name: Squalls and fog
milestones.log: Fog rolls in, the ships slow down, and the keeper has to light the fog bell too. It is harder now, but kind: nobody sinks, they only wait.

milestones.name: Sound and music
milestones.log: Added the creak of the stairs, the wind at the gallery and a small tune on an accordion. The game feels like a place now.

milestones.name: Release: Tiny Lighthouse 1.0
milestones.log: Published Tiny Lighthouse 1.0 from a harbour café, with a slow connection and a fast heart. Kind messages are arriving. A few people even bought it.

tasks.name: Add a tiny feature
tasks.question: What should the keeper be able to do next?
choices: Collect every seashell on the island
done: The keeper waves. Ships wave back. Small, and exactly right.
The juggling is impressive, if rather off-topic.
The seashell counter now reaches 4,000. Perhaps too many shells.

tasks.name: Fix a funny bug
tasks.question: The ships sail backwards when the moon is full. Where do you look first?
done: Found it: the tide pulled the ships home stern first. Fixed, with a small sigh of pride.
The sails are now a lovely blue. The ships still sail backwards.
The hat is fine. The ships are not. The search continues.

tasks.name: Balance the game
tasks.question: Playtesters say the storms are too hard. What do you change?
choices: Make the light reach a little further
Make the ships faster in every weather
done: A little further, and suddenly every storm is a good story rather than a bad day.
Without storms it is calm. Perhaps a little too calm.
The ships now zip about like dragonflies. Fun, but odd.

tasks.name: Arrange the scene
tasks.question: Where should the lighthouse stand on the title screen?
choices: On the rocks, a little to the left, with the sea in front
Right in the middle, very large
done: The title screen breathes now: rocks, sea and a light that waits for you.
Very large indeed. It looks surprised.
Mysterious. Nobody can find the lighthouse.

tasks.name: Prepare a small update
tasks.question: What goes into the update notes?
choices: What changed, in plain words, and a thank-you
A thousand words about the code
Nothing at all: let them guess
done: Short, clear and kind notes. Players will like that.
The notes are longer than the game.
